clauses.text: An Ultrastable system is an organization of virtual managers and staff that runs itself on a server-side clock and closes its own loops. A person writes one file, IDEA.md; everything after that is the system's work.

It is for something that has to keep running. An idea qualifies only when all four hold: a loop it must close, a measure that can be wrong, upkeep and improvement that never end, and a running cost the owner accepts. The bootstrapper refuses anything else before it hires a role or provisions anything.

Autonomous means the system has self-referential loops and the ability to close them. Every loop has a trigger, an owner, a closing probe and a write-back, and every open item has an owner, a trigger and a probe.

The owner supplies direction, the idea and a budget. The system does the back end: errors, credentials, deploys, retries and repairs, recorded where the owner can audit them and never handed to the owner to act on.

Everything runs server-side: a Cloudflare Worker with its own D1 database and cron, and GitHub Actions on its built-in token. Nothing depends on a person's computer, a desktop app or an open chat session.

probe: grep:agents/AGENTS.md::If it is not in code, it does not exist
clauses.text: If it is not in code, it does not exist. The repository and the database are the only memory; chat, tool memory and documents nothing reads are not storage.

The heartbeat is one tick every 10 minutes from the Worker's cron. A second producer, POST /pulse/watch, runs a tick when the newest one is older than two intervals, so one silent trigger never stops the clock.

A tick runs every step listed below, and the same cron runs the loops listed after them. A failing step is recorded and filed as work, and the other steps still run. Each tick writes its report to tick_runs and /health.
Work is items with a claim, a prediction logged before the change and a closing probe after it. An item leaves the active set only with a disposition; reconcile reopens any that left without one.

The only pause is the interrupt gate: a step that is irreversible and identity-bound with no reversible path. It becomes one gate card with a default in effect and a closing probe; the system works on in the meantime.
One halt stops every recurring path: the Worker variable HALT=1 stops the cron, the watch route and the webhooks. Pages keep serving.
Every model call is paid from the owner's monthly budget through one governor; the budget is a number in the repository, never a promise.
bootstrap/bootstrap.py runs the stages below in order. It is idempotent: running it again changes nothing that is already true.
A stage that cannot finish is recorded as blocked with its reason and becomes a backlog item with a closing probe; the boot continues with the next stage. A missing credential never stops the boot.
The boot is accepted only when the system's own drills show at least a year unattended (year_gate) and its /health answers live (verify_live).

From its first deploy every system serves all of its public surfaces together: a web page with the Built on Ultrastable footer, /health, the discovery manifest, the knowledge graph's read side, and a listing in the ultrastable.io directory. No gate may hide one of them.
A system needs no key from its owner when it is hosted: the platform deploys it through its own OIDC route and gives it its repository from the seed.

The system reads its own stage every tick from evidence it recorded itself; nothing is declared. A stage is reached when the reading holds for it and every stage below, and lost when it stops holding. The first unmet stage is filed as IGNITE-<stage> with the numbers that block it, and only the same reading closes it.
Bootstrapped means instrumented or above: the system stands, runs and measures itself. Critical and self-sustaining are the two stages above that.

Criticality is a number. k_eff = (credited verified deploys + credited loop-originated items) / (spend units + human touches) over the window. The system is critical when k_eff stays at or above k_min, and self-sustaining when it stays critical with no open ignition gaps and no human touches.
Self-reference is the multiplier: k_self counts only deploys the system originated and shipped on itself. A deploy an outside session drove raises k_eff, never k_self.
The standing goal is a year unattended: a simulated 10th-percentile horizon of at least 365 days, with every fault class it names drilled against the real recovery code.

Trust is computed per surface and action class from recorded outcomes, and widens scope only through a reviewed change to autonomy/policy.json. Trust never reaches the interrupt gate, secrets or harness permissions.

ignition.about: the starting point: nothing recorded yet
the schema this code needs exists and at least one role can take work
the heartbeat completed every step for min_streak ticks in a row and missed no slot in the last hour
every loop is ticking and good-slot coverage over 24 h is at least min_coverage (LOOPPROOF-1), watched by a second producer
the system closed items with independently verified outcomes in the window, with no silent drop
every objective has a probe-backed target and no metric is only declared
k_eff has been at or above k_min for min_streak ticks in a row
critical for sustained_ticks, with 0 open ignition gaps and 0 human touches

loops.about: KILL-SWITCH-1: once a day the global switch is turned on, checked, turned off in every case and the test recorded
loops.name: kill-drill

loops.about: AUTH-1: refresh runs first so nothing lapses
loops.name: credentials

loops.about: LIVE-FRESH-2: own early step; inside the sweeper it ran after 32 of 46 subrequests were spent and never wrote, so /live froze
loops.name: live-changes

loops.about: PROGRESS-1: the other repositories, at most hourly each
loops.name: fleet-changes

loops.about: SUBSTANCE-1: two merged PRs per pass are classified from their diff, so trivial merges never count as progress
loops.name: substance

loops.about: STICKY-1: freshness, breadth, depth and diversity of every system's content; a stale or thin one files STICKY-<system>, and its unpromoted entries become the social queue
loops.name: stickiness

loops.about: DATAGRAPH-1: every table of this system's own D1 becomes a graph (rows are nodes, references and mentioned ids are edges), kept bi-temporally; hubs, communities, bridges and orphans are read each pass
loops.name: knowledge-graph

loops.about: KGRAPH-AI-1: embeddings, extracted relations and community summaries on new graph nodes, scaled by the spend throttle
loops.name: graph-ai

loops.about: PROGRESS-1: release cadence monitor; a slow system has its producers dispatched, a stalled one files STALL-<system>
loops.name: progress

loops.about: LIVE-FRESH-2: a stale published snapshot re-dispatches its own publisher
loops.name: freshness

loops.about: GH-ONLY-WATCH-1: GitHub-only loops get a second clock and go live the hour Pages turns on
loops.name: gh-only

loops.about: TENANT-DEPLOY-1: a tenant repository's merge ships within the hour (twice an hour, ~4 subrequests)
loops.name: tenant-deploy

loops.about: every tenant back end has a second route to run besides its own cron
loops.name: tenant-pulse

loops.about: D1-SNAPSHOT-1: the daily copy of D1 into the AUDIT bucket, read back before it counts
loops.name: cost-samples

rules.title: The user does the idea; the system does the backend; one fix improves every system
One tenant row admits a tenant; every registry is derived
Words match code
Vision: systems, not one-off apps
Drain to zero, fleetwide
Interview-first, voice-first, pill-shaped input
No zombie branches or PRs; every loop gets better
Complete everything; close everything
Merge and deploy everything automatically; clean up everywhere
Complete all work; drain every issue; merge every PR; zero manual intervention
Automation never discards unmerged work
Strange loops: every loop closes itself and improves itself; no zombie sessions
Clockwork: every loop is a clock, and a stopped or inaccurate clock is not a working clock
Every loop declares its flows and closes its feedback
Growth: the product manager's job is growth, not only bug fixes
Analytics are a feedback loop, built on Cloudflare, never on an opt-in tag
Time and iteration are part of the system; a snapshot hides what a series shows
The owner console is an agent, not a command parser
Scout the state of the art; keep improving
R&D and competitive analysis are the product manager's job, as code
Autonomous audit, remediation and improvement; Quniverse parity
Every failure mode is audited and every finding is taken by the queue
Mantra, as code
Self-reference is the multiplier
The system knows what the user does not know
Server side owns every loop; a client never closes one
Code agents produce; Ultrastable owns
Point and click, always; never ask a person to handle a credential
Every action only the owner can take is one link
Meta content is a signal; the microphone is monitored
One design language, many products; design is enforced and experimented, never left to chance
One halt stops everything; nothing is exempt
Provenance is first-class: every input and change records where it came from and what it did
Words match code; code checks it
The UI/UX manager is a closed loop: the front end does not drift into a mishmash
Core is the system of record; tenants are test beds
Every tenant app lives in its own repository
Every deployment is a sandboxed tenant
Every system deploys itself in full: repo, back end and a public web UI
Everything is traceable, and the database stays small
The front end is always backed by the back end
One repository standard, applied at creation and every day
Every manager is a running loop that owns code
One map, one manifest, no hand-copied mirrors
Both start paths are user stories that run
Every reference a rule names resolves
Standards are measured, with a decision per standard
One standard for every tenant repository; one scaffold writes it, one check reads it
Every repository says where its code runs
One contract for every system; statements hold front to back and back to front
Every decision is measured
The system sets its own goals and turns its own knobs
A vector space and a knowledge graph in every system; novel connections are generated, not waited for
Every system keeps a knowledge graph of all its data, built and maintained automatically
Ultrastable runs its own R&D and publishes its own white papers; Ashby's mechanism is code
Thought leadership is a loop: every paper becomes posts that carry the hook
The social module is how a system faces humans
A year unattended is simulated, not asserted; the system does what it says
Every system gives people a reason to come back
Public by default, discoverable always
Anyone can launch; no code agent, terminal or key
Suggested ideas are broad and living, not single-field
Automate back-end and front-end development; improve on its own
Every system updates itself and the platform
Red-team the system's own blind spots; the owner should never find a failure first
A repository the system writes stays small enough for the system to maintain; split by rate of change and owner, not by topic
Today's failures are guarded in code, not remembered
Blind spots are measured, not assumed safe
The owner's words are the input; what stays true is the output
Issue inflow never exceeds closures; every issue inside its SLA
Find another path before asking; the information is already held
Everything bootstraps itself from a cold start and works together from birth
Root-caused on launch day
Open standards, never a home-grown format
Every surface works together from the first deploy; one command proves it
Every system carries its own definition, generated from its code
A fresh seed proves the whole; no surface contradicts the axiom
Large work is planned and worked in steps on the server
Every piece of work has one server-side record
Large change is phased: audit, coverage, implement, verify, fix, integrate, final gate
Ashby's journal runs as kernel mechanisms
Every document is consumed by code
Closed loops only; nobody reads, reviews or decides
No made-up numbers
Work items an agent cannot misread; done means proven live
Apply open standards; do not reinvent formats
Introduce the work; do not wait to be found
Strategy and promotion are the system's job
Promotion is part of every app's and tenant's role
The system knows what the owner does not
Question what the system does not know; the solution space must keep growing
All information is useful somehow; ingest it, keep the record in files, audit the surfaces
Only behaviour counts; no illusion of productivity
Visible progress at every visit, for six months with no input
A year unattended, measured
Nothing sits in the queue; every item gets a coded disposition
No open items, ever
A seed is not done until it runs a year unattended
A seed that answers is not yet a seed that runs itself
The template is code only

tagline: Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

tick_steps.about: MIGRATE-SELF-1: apply pending D1 migrations through the tick's own binding (no credential), ledgered in _migrations.
tick_steps.name: migrate

tick_steps.about: Every item that left the active set has a disposition; items whose trigger is done become ready.
tick_steps.name: reconcile

tick_steps.about: Claims with no heartbeat for claim_ttl_minutes are released so work never stalls.
tick_steps.name: reap_claims

tick_steps.about: CONNECTOR-HEALTH-1: every linked connector is read each tick (no new cron): last_ok, expires_at and the result of the refresh attempt refreshDue made just before this tick. A connector whose last two refresh attempts both failed raises one
tick_steps.name: connector_health

tick_steps.about: Gate cards close themselves when their probe shows the owner's step is done.
tick_steps.name: probe_gates

tick_steps.about: Predictions due now are graded against built-in metrics.
tick_steps.name: score_predictions

tick_steps.about: OBJECTIVES-1: read every metric through its probe. Outside its healthy condition it files its own remedy item (owner, done check, closing probe) and closes that item when the probe passes again. A new system gets grace_hours before liveness
tick_steps.name: measure

tick_steps.about: Trust per (surface, action_class) from recorded outcomes; a crossed threshold opens a ladder PR item.
tick_steps.name: accrue_trust

tick_steps.about: SELFAUDIT-1: probe the failure-mode register; red files or reopens FM-<id>, green closes it with evidence.
tick_steps.name: selfaudit

tick_steps.about: UNKNOWNS-1: question what the system does not know; the questions are plus items. GOALS-1: read every goal, sample it, move at most one knob per goal toward its target, review earlier moves, propose stretch goals, retire stale ones.
tick_steps.name: goals

tick_steps.about: PLAN-1: turn the goal furthest out of bounds into a task tree (audit > implement > verify > fix > integrate > gate), advance live plans, turn knobs itself, and gate each plan on a fresh reading of its goal. "Better" means a measured goal mo
tick_steps.name: plan

tick_steps.about: Roles whose tick is due pull the top ready item for their role and get a dispatch row.
tick_steps.name: dispatch

tick_steps.about: DOER-1: every claimed item ends done, parked with a reason, or waiting with its claim kept; nothing is left for the reaper to release unworked.
tick_steps.name: execute

tick_steps.about: Plus share over the last 20 closed items; below target opens a rebalance item for the portfolio manager.
tick_steps.name: check_plus_share

tick_steps.about: Q-PARITY-4 (SLA-120M): an item open past 120 minutes is raised to the top, and the cause is filed once a day; nothing ages silently. One indexed COUNT-first read (status, created_at); the per-item work only runs when the count is above zero
tick_steps.name: age_sla

tick_steps.about: Q-COST-PROOF-2 (cost-probe): once a day, only while the free tier is ok, turn each breached cost sample into a queue item. It adds one indexed read per budget and nothing when the account is degraded (FREE_TIER_WIDE_STEPS), so it can never
tick_steps.name: cost_probe

tick_steps.about: LOOPPROOF-1: every loop's expected slots against the slots it ran in; a loop that did not run files MISSED-<loop>.
tick_steps.name: pulse

tick_steps.about: CRITICALITY-1: k_eff over the rolling window; a tick may not end idle or under k_min without originating the highest-value item at the head.
tick_steps.name: criticality

tick_steps.about: BOOT-KNOWS-1: the stage from bootstrap to criticality, read from the system's own tables; the first unmet stage is IGNITE-<stage>.
tick_steps.name: ignition
